senses.gloss:
(I)--a daughter of दक्ष, and wife of कश्यप.
1: भा. III. १४. 7; वा. ६६. ५४; Vi. I. १५. १२४, १४०.
Her sons generally known as Daityas. Mother of हिरण्याक्ष and हिरण्यकशिपु.
2: भा. VI. 6. २५; १८. ११; VII. 1. ३९; Br. III. 3. ५६; M. 6. 1-8; वा. ६७. ४९.
Mother of Dantavaktra by the sage's curse.
3: भा. IX. २४. ३७.
Her sons प्रह्लाद and Hari were devotees of Hari.
4: Ib. VI. १८. १०.
Always set her mind on truth;
5: Ib. VII. 2. ६१.
daughter सिम्हिका;
5: a) वा. ६७. ६०.
(आदित्य्-वा। प्।). Finding her sons slain by Hari to help Indra, she became enraged, and asked her husband to bless her with a child to kill Indra. The un- willing husband offered it on condition of her observing certain vows for १०० years. So she observed them and Indra came to assist her. One day he found her sleep- ing in an unorthodox posture and entering her womb cut the embryo into seven and then into ४९ pieces; but at her request he gave all of them the status of gods, known as Maruts.
6: भा. VI. १८. २३-77; Br. I. 1. ११२; ch. 5 (whole); 7. ४६५; IV. 9. 3; M. 6. ४७; ch. 7 (whole); वा. ६७. ८६, १३५; Vi. I. २१. ३०-41.
Impelled by passion and desire for children she approached her husband one evening for sexual intercourse. कश्यप said that it was the hour when शिवगणस् moved about and for him, to offer the शन्ध्य-prayer. But she persisted and gained her object. She however requested to be redeemed of the sin. कश्यप [page२-088+ ३४] remarked that since she approached him at the wrong time, her sons would have पैशाच-character and would be killed by Hari. For her penitence she was blessed with a righteous child among her grandsons.
7: भा. III. १४ (whole).
Held the तेजस् in embryo for a hundred years when darkness enveloped all directions. The two door-keepers of वैकुण्ठ cursed by seers for preventing them from having दर्सन् of Hari were born as her two sons, when there were evil omens.
8: Ib. VI. १५. 1-१०; १६. ३५; १७. 2-१५.
Prayed for another son. This was वज्रान्ग who on his birth accord- ing to her orders bound Indra. The latter was released on the mediation of ब्रह्मा and कश्यप.
9: M. १४६. १८-55; १७१. २९.
Mother of Daityas; a Mother Goddess to be worshipped in house and palace buildings
